answer: Identity is bound to a signed measurement of the runtime that produced it, so two identities reporting the same measurement are counted as one voice no matter how many keys or balances sit behind them. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. The reef is the quoted measurement, the relic the group it forms, and the beacon the voice that group is worth; the reef and the relic collapse a farm, while only a fresh beacon of hardware escapes the grouping. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
